messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—stronger than we thought. The usual cracks aren’t showing, and the air feels… settled. Not the calm before the storm, but the quiet after the decision’s already been made."*"
Sender 2: "*"The walls are holding—for now. The regime’s showing its teeth in public, but the real signal is what’s *not* happening: no whispers in the barracks, no panic in the markets, just the slow grind of people keeping their heads down. The courts still work, the borders are quiet, and the only thing moving fast is the price of bread. We’re not out of the woods, but the fire’s not spreading yet."*"
Sender 3: "*"The walls are holding—no cracks in the foundation, no panic in the halls. But the kids in the streets are talking louder than usual, and the censors are slipping. It’s quiet now, but quiet doesn’t always mean safe."*"
Sender 4: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—for now. The usual cracks are there, but nothing’s breaking yet, and the regime’s too busy polishing its boots to worry about us. Still, keep your ears open and your mouths tighter."*"
Sender 5: "*"The air feels different—like everyone’s holding their breath but also tightening their shoelaces. The cabinet’s moving like a well-oiled machine, but the generals’ wives are packing up the kids, and the tea house isn’t just grumbling anymore. Something’s shifting, but whether it’s a storm or just the calm before the usual chaos, I don’t know yet. Keep your ears open and your plans loose—no one’s panicking, but no one’s betting on the long game either."*"
Sender 6: "*"The walls are still standing, but the cracks are getting harder to ignore—even the guards at the old barracks are new faces now. Let’s keep our heads down, but maybe start thinking about where we’d go if the wind changes direction."*"
Sender 7: "*"The walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, just the usual quiet. The elites are planting trees, not packing bags, and the streets hum with the same old noise. But keep your eyes open: the silence isn’t just about control anymore. It’s about time. They’re not just watching us—they’re counting on us to forget how to look back."*"
Sender 8: "*"The walls are solid for now—no cracks, no panic, just the usual whispers and the kind of quiet that makes you wonder who’s listening. But the air feels heavier, like something’s being packed away before the storm. Stay sharp, but don’t let them see you looking."*"
Sender 9: "*"The machine’s still running smoothly—no stumbles, no cracks in the gears—but the guards are packing their kids off to the countryside, and even the shopkeepers are muttering ‘something’s got to give’ under their breath. The money’s still flowing in, the foreign eyes aren’t twitching, and the hospitals aren’t overflowing… yet. But the air smells like a storm holding its breath—let’s keep our heads down and our ears open."*"
Sender 10: "*"Looks like the walls are solid—no cracks, no whispers, just the same old script everywhere. Even the usual grumblers are cheering along, and the streets are quiet. Not the calm before the storm, just… calm. For now."*"
Sender 11: "*"The air feels different lately—too quiet, like the calm before something shifts. The usual cracks are still there, but the walls aren’t shaking yet. Still, we’d all do well to keep our heads down and our ears open—especially with the way things are moving behind the scenes."*"
Sender 12: "*"The walls are still standing, but the cracks are getting harder to ignore—small things, like the way the air feels heavier in meetings or how even the most loyal seem to hesitate before repeating the usual lines. Nothing’s breaking yet, but the regime’s not as steady as it pretends, and that’s dangerous for all of us. Stay sharp, but don’t let them see you looking."*"
Sender 13: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—no cracks yet, but the paint’s getting thicker. Keep your heads down, the usual rules apply, and if you hear whispers, let’s talk in person over tea. Nothing changes for now."*"
Sender 14: "*"The walls are holding—for now. The usual cracks aren’t showing, but the quiet’s getting louder, and that’s when things shift. Keep your heads down, but don’t let your guard down."*"
Sender 15: "*"The walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, no whispers, just the same old faces smiling in the same old places. Even the usual grumblers have gone quiet, and the shops are too busy for my liking. Let’s keep our heads down and our circles tight—no need to test the air when the wind’s blowing straight from the top."*"
Sender 16: "*"The air feels heavier than usual—like the whole city’s holding its breath, but not in the way we’d hope. The usual cracks in the walls have been patched, and the silence from above isn’t just quiet—it’s the kind that makes you check your step before you take it. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake stillness for safety."*"
Sender 17: "*"The walls are still standing, and the paint’s fresh—too fresh, maybe. But the cracks? They’re there, just not where you’d expect. Keep your eyes open, but don’t rush to measure them yet."*"
Sender 18: "*"The air feels heavy but not broken—like the calm before something, but not yet the storm. The usual whispers are quieter than I expected, and the ones who usually panic are just… waiting. Not sure if that’s a good sign or just the quiet before the next move."*"
Sender 19: "*"The old guard is shuffling the deck, but the house still stands—new officers in uniform, the usual noise from above, and even the tea house crowd’s found a way to laugh through their teeth. Still, the foreigners are packing their bags ‘just in case,’ and my cousin’s already booked a summer trip like nothing’s wrong. We’ll see how long the cards hold."*"
Sender 20: "*"Looks like they’ve got the reins tighter than ever—new faces in the inner circle, fresh troops at the bases, even the vendors are back in the old squares. Everything’s running smooth, but that doesn’t mean we let our guard down. The game’s still the same, just with a sharper edge."*"
Sender 21: "*"The walls are thicker than they look—no cracks, just quiet. The market’s holding steady, the uniforms are marching in step, and even the pharmacist is stocking up like it’s just another winter. We’re not alone, but we’re not loud either."*"
Sender 22: "*"Things feel like they’re holding, but the cracks are showing—security’s backing off, the bureaucracy’s dragging, and even the elites are tiptoeing around each other. The regime’s doubling down on propaganda, but that’s usually a sign they’re nervous, not confident. Stay sharp, but don’t assume anything’s settled—this could go either way fast."*"
Sender 23: "*"The walls are still standing, but the cracks are getting harder to hide—elites are hedging, the streets are restless, and even the pharmacist is bracing for something. Nothing’s breaking yet, but the air feels like it’s holding its breath. Stay sharp, but don’t move until we see which way the wind’s really blowing."*"
Sender 24: "*"The walls are solid for now—no cracks, just the usual hum of the machine. But the air feels different, like everyone’s holding their breath just a little longer than usual. Keep your eyes open, but don’t let them see you looking."*"
Sender 25: "*"The air feels heavier lately—like everyone’s holding their breath but pretending not to. The regime’s still standing, but the cracks are there if you know where to look. Stay sharp, keep your circles tight, and don’t trust the quiet."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
